findings.evidence: <select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required=""> <select id="dob-month-select" autocomplete="bday-month" required=""> <select id="dob-year-select" autocomplete="bday-year" required="">
findings.fix: Use three short text fields for day, month and year, with the numeric input mode.
findings.violation: A date the person knows by heart is picked from three drop-downs, the year from 60 options.

findings.evidence: The form's heading is 'Create your account' and its submit button reads 'Create account', yet it requires #street-input (street address), #website-input (company website), #member-input (an existing 8-digit membership number), #acctnum-input (an existing account number), #postal-input, #shipspeed-select (preferred shipping speed), #legalname-input (a second 'Your name' field after #name-input's 'Full name'), #org-input (organization name), #contacttime-input (preferred contact time), and the #row-dob fieldset (date of birth), none of which account creation uses.
findings.fix: Drop fields the account-creation task does not use (shipping speed, organization name, preferred contact time, date of birth, company website), remove the duplicate name question, and drop membership/account-number fields that presuppose an account the person is still trying to create; ask any field a later step genuinely needs at that step instead.
findings.violation: The form requires many fields its stated task, creating an account, cannot use: it asks for a legal/account-holder's name twice (#name-input and #legalname-input), and requires a membership number and an account number before the account that would carry them exists, alongside shipping, organization, contact-time and birth-date fields unrelated to signing up.

findings.evidence: <input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="" size="3"> (size=3)
findings.fix: Size the field to show at least 5 characters.
findings.violation: This postal code field shows 3 characters, too few to show a typical value whole while it is typed and checked.

findings.fix: Loosen the pattern to accept every valid way of writing the value, and normalise it after submission.
findings.violation: The pattern on this phone field rejects valid values such as +44 20 7946 0958; 020 7946 0958.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>, sitting between #row-contacttime and the #row-dob fieldset, while #submit-btn, the form's primary action at the end of the document, carries no declared style at all.
findings.fix: Move 'View details' out of the field column (or after the primary submit) and give the primary submit at least as much visual weight as this button, instead of leaving it unstyled.
findings.violation: A secondary action sits above fields that have not been filled in yet (the date-of-birth selects), and it is given explicit padding and font-size while the primary 'Create account' submit has no declared styling, so the secondary action is more prominent than the primary one.

findings.evidence: font-size: 13px declared by its inline style
findings.fix: Set the field's font size to at least 16 pixels.
findings.violation: The text in this field is 13 pixels, below the 16 pixels at which a phone stops zooming the page on focus.
This web address field is type text, so a phone does not show the keyboard built for it.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>: 16px text at a default line-height plus 12px of padding above and below gives a rendered height of roughly 40 CSS pixels.
findings.fix: Increase the button's vertical padding so its rendered height reaches about 44 CSS pixels.
findings.violation: This button's declared padding and font-size put its rendered height at roughly 40 CSS pixels, short of the roughly 44 pixels mobile-usability guidance recommends for a fingertip target.
